paper.title_en: Self-Consistent Subtracted Second Quasiparticle Random-Phase Approximation for Dipole Responses in Neutron-Rich Oxygen Isotopes
paper.abstract_en: Describing the nuclear dipole response in open-shell nuclei across wide energy scales, from low-lying states below the neutron separation energy to giant resonances near 30MeV, within a single microscopic framework is a long-standing open problem. Here we establish, for the first time, a self-consistent subtracted second quasiparticle random-phase approximation (SSQRPA) that simultaneously incorporates pairing correlations (HF+BCS), explicit two-quasiparticle (2qp) and four-quasiparticle (4qp) configurations in a large model space, the full forward- and backward-going QRPA structure, and a subtraction procedure to eliminate double counting and ensure stability. No existing framework unifies all of these ingredients in the quasiparticle basis. We apply SSQRPA to the dipole excitations of neutron-rich oxygen isotopes $^{18,20,22}$O, where the standard QRPA fails to simultaneously account for high-energy giant dipole resonance (GDR) states near 22--25MeV, medium-energy GDR states in the 10--18MeV region, and isolated low-lying $1^-$ states below the neutron separation energy. In SSQRPA, the dominant isovector (IV) GDR strength shifts downward by approximately 4MeV into the experimentally observed medium-energy region, while the compressional isoscalar (IS) GDR strength remains concentrated at higher energies, in qualitative agreement with the observed electromagnetic dissociation cross sections. For the low-lying states, the root-mean-square deviation from experiment is reduced from 5.31MeV (QRPA) to 0.35MeV (SSQRPA) in $^{18}$O, and from 4.07MeV to 0.74MeV in $^{20}$O, demonstrating that 4qp correlations are essential for a simultaneous description of dipole excitations over a wide range of excitation energies. The SSQRPA provides a powerful and general framework for future microscopic studies of collective excitations in open-shell nuclei across the nuclear mass table.
